Subject: Recap & next steps: inference cost / latency qualification for Stellar Bio

Hi Alicia — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of what we captured
- Workload: customer-facing research assistant + batch embedding jobs for analytics. Mostly chat (streaming) with intermittent large-batch embed runs.
- Estimated monthly token range (your estimate): 250M — 600M tokens / month.
- Latency SLOs: interactive chat target ~p50 < 70ms, p95 < 200ms for the majority of queries. Batch embed jobs can tolerate higher latency.
- Budget guidance you gave: target $/1M tokens ~ $900 (goal), monthly budget band $15k — $40k.

Latency vs cost considerations we discussed
- Streaming + dedicated low-latency tier is the simplest path to meet the chat SLOs but costs more per token.
- Batching & prefix caching for embeddings can drive unit cost down significantly on Dedicated / Private.
- Hybrid route: streaming on Hosted for small volume + Dedicated reserved for heavy bursts and embeddings.

Proposed next steps
1) We’ll send an initial pricing model with 3 scenarios (Hosted, Dedicated reserve, Hybrid) and estimated $/1M tokens at your 250M and 600M volume points. (See attached pricing_model_stellar_v1.xlsx)
2) SE deep-dive / prompt sampling session (Marissa) to validate latency numbers and exact prompt shape (2–3 hours).
3) Procurement intro + draft SOW for a 6-week pilot (option to extend to 6 months).

Request for you
- Please confirm the token volume range and whether the embedding jobs are batched daily or ad-hoc.
- Share procurement contact if you want us to send a pilot quote / SOW directly.

I’ll loop Marissa to schedule the SE session. Thanks — excited to keep this moving.

Best,

Thanks Rafael — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side:
- Token volumes: 250M is our conservative projection for Q1 usage if pilot converts; 600M is our internal growth scenario if adoption is strong.
- Embedding cadence: batch jobs run nightly for analytics (~2–3M tokens per run), but occasionally we run larger one-off bulk runs (up to ~30M tokens).
- Budget: procurement target is to keep unit cost under $1,000 / 1M tokens, ideally closer to $900 if performance is comparable.
- Latency: chat must feel real-time for researchers — p50 < 70ms is critical; p95 under 200ms is negotiable but preferred.

Procurement contact: procurement@stellarbio.com (they handle quotes and PO terms). Please send any pilot SOW + quote to that address.

Hi Alicia — Marissa (SE) here. Quick notes from an SE perspective and a couple of concrete scenarios so you have numbers to work with for procurement.

Key technical levers that impact unit economics
- Batching (larger batch sizes for embeddings) — reduces per-token GPU overhead for bulk runs.
- Prefix / KV caching for chat — can reduce repeated token decode/encode cost for common prompts (~10–15% typical).
- Quantization & model selection — switching to a quantized variant (where acceptable) reduces runtime cost but may impact latency slightly.

Two example pricing scenarios (ballpark estimates for Stella workload)
1) Hosted streaming (no reserved capacity) — Simple onboarding, higher unit price.
   - Estimated unit: ~$1,200 / 1M tokens at 250M/mo; ~$1,050 / 1M at 600M/mo (volume discount).
   - Pros: fastest time-to-value; cons: less predictable cost.

2) Dedicated reserved capacity (3-month pilot / 6-month commit) — optimized for steady throughput + caching.
   - Assumptions: dedicated pool with batching enabled + prefix caching; moderate quantization on embeddings.
   - Estimated unit: ~$650 — $750 / 1M tokens at 250M/mo profile; ~$550 — $700 / 1M at 600M/mo depending on caching effectiveness.
   - With a conservative prefix cache reduction of 12% (per your ask) effective token consumption drops and unit cost improves by ~10–12% compared to the base.

Recommended approach
- Pilot on Dedicated reserved with a short hosted fallback route: this gives a predictable baseline for procurement, while still allowing streaming tests in hosted mode.
- SE session: we’ll run a small prompt set against both Hosted streaming and Dedicated (same model) to measure p50/p95 and validate caching benefit.

Next steps I’ll take this week
- Draft a 6-week pilot SOW and a pricing sheet that shows both the Hosted and Dedicated scenarios, clearly call out the caching assumptions and the $/1M numbers. (Attaching SOW_template_stellar.docx)
- Schedule a 2-hour SE session — Rafael, can you propose three time slots?

Cheers,
Marissa
